newsitem.title: USA: CME LUMBER FUTURES END WITH PARED GAINS.
newsitem.headline: CME LUMBER FUTURES END WITH PARED GAINS.

text.p: CME lumber futures eased from best levels but closed mostly higher following the posting of higher than expected cash spruce prices, traders said.
Lumber closed $1.00 per tbf lower to $6.00 higher with only January off. September ended up $4.20 at $356.50 and November up $1.00 at $349.00 per tbf.

Larger than expected gains in cash spruce prices this week sparked the early rally but futures again ran into resistance and drifted back by the close. Although some traders see further gains in cash on building mill order files, others cited continued availability of wood for immediate shipment.
Some mills have their wood sold out front while others are looking for more orders. Demand for species were also mixed as southern pine prices were actually lower, they said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $352 per tbf, up $8 from midweek and up $12 from last Friday. They said prices were mixed, with the Random Lengths Framing Lumber Commposite down $1 for the week.
